nodes.dialogue_text: Enough! I have watched this slaughter for nine days. Your grandfather decimates your army while you hold back out of filial piety. If you will not end this, I will!

Then the Lord of the Worlds leapt from the chariot, his yellow garments billowing like a sun descending to earth. He seized the Sudarshana Chakra and strode toward Bhishma, the very ground trembling beneath His feet.
Come, O Keshava! Come! To fall by Your hand would be the supreme honour. Let this wretched life end in the embrace of the Lord Himself. I welcome You!

Madhava, stop! You swore an oath — no weapons! The world watches. If You break Your word, what hope remains for dharma? I will do it. I swear to you — tomorrow, Bhishma falls. By my hand. Please... return to the chariot.

choices.choice_text: [Let Krishna advance. Bhishma dies by divine hand.]
[Pull Krishna back. Swear the oath to fell Bhishma tomorrow.]

nodes.dialogue_text: ...Very well, Partha. I will hold. But mark my words — tomorrow, there will be no mercy. No hesitation. You will place Shikhandi before you, and you will strike without pause until the Patriarch falls.
The cosmic order fractures. Krishna Vasudeva has broken His sacred vow. The weight of adharma ripples across the battlefield. Time itself recoils. This path cannot hold.
